rationale: The challenge correctly notes that an unobservable perception miss or timing violation defeats runtime assurance. However, the claim itself explicitly defines safety as conditional, stating that the formalization establishes safety 'only under explicit safe-start, monitor/timing, recovery-state and reversionary-controller premises.' The Plaidypvs inference rule in S-EVID-005 (slides 7-8) formally requires these exact premises: initial safe state, timed monitor bounds on advanced controller execution, carry-over recovery condition G, and verified reversionary controller execution. The claim and its artifact uses strictly preserve these conditionality boundaries.
evidence_locators: S-EVID-005, PDF pp. 5-8, Plaidypvs rule and premises
S-EVID-005, PDF pp. 8-12, Productive conflict avoidance example and timing/dynamics assumptions
limitations: Inspection is based on the 14-page NASA DASC 2024 presentation slides; full formal PVS proof scripts and physical flight/sensor implementations were not evaluated.
